java_locations: tim/builtin/IntVal.java#executeReturnFunction: Integer.parseInt(values.get(0).toString()), and on NumberFormatException the TIM error 'Cannot convert S to integer.'

java/lang/Integer.java#parseInt(String,int) (JDK 21): empty string fails; a first char below '0' must be '-' (limit Integer.MIN_VALUE) or '+' and must not be the whole string; each following UTF-16 unit is converted with Character.digit(char, 10), and a negative digit fails; the value is accumulated negatively with the multmin and limit+digit checks, so -2147483648 parses and 2147483648 fails.

java/lang/Character.java#digit(char,int): for radix 10 a char is a digit when its general category is Nd (DECIMAL_DIGIT_NUMBER) and the result is its decimal value; a surrogate unit is never a digit, so supplementary Nd digits fail.
causal_divergence: str::parse::<i32> agrees with Integer.parseInt on sign and overflow but rejects every non-ASCII Nd digit, so %intval("+１２３") and Devanagari or Arabic-Indic digits are fatal TIM errors in Rust and integers in Java.
invariant: %intval accepts exactly the strings Integer.parseInt(s, 10) accepts, giving the same value: an optional single leading '+' or '-', then one or more BMP Nd units, each worth its decimal value, with Java's overflow bounds.
planned_change: Replace text.parse::<i32>() with java_parse_int, a direct port of Integer.parseInt(s, 10) over UTF-16 units. Character.digit(char, 10) becomes a table of the 37 BMP Nd zero code points in Unicode 15.0; each run of ten has consecutive values. Error text is unchanged.
